steps.what: Define job specifications from verified site constraints and selected energy improvements
Prepare job specification sheets by transferring the verified technical content
Check and release the exact energy improvement specification sheets

tasks.design: Configure a {DOCS} specification template to place the auditor's verified requirements and dimensions into consistent sheets. The auditor retains technical content decisions and final issue; no template selects equipment, invents dimensions or approves installation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specification content is retyped and formatted after technical decisions are made.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document fields can reuse explicit, checked requirements.
tasks.still_hard: Interfaces between measures, hidden construction details and scope exclusions.
tasks.human_edge: Define requirements that installers can interpret safely and consistently.
tasks.altitude: Less document assembly; technical specification authority remains unchanged.

reach.learn: Traceable dimensions, performance requirements and exclusions

evidence.claim: A native specification-sheet generator using verified content is plausible model knowledge; the digest does not document technical specification automation or a labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is specification content and sheet preparation after measure selection and feasibility analysis. Prior site measurement and feasibility work are counted once elsewhere, not repeated as new capture here.

Auditor produces project/measure IDs, location, verified dimensions and units, required performance, material requirements, interfaces, exclusions, evidence references and revision in s1. Its full 50 hours include checking and entering these fields. Missing dimensions or bespoke requirements stay manual; the generator leaves gaps visible.
Auditor maintains the approved template with five additional upkeep hours. Test native document fields before custom code; existing generated sheets earn no new labour saving.
research_questions: Can template output preserve every interface requirement without extra clarification from installers?

approvals.approved_version: Exact sheet revision, dimensions, units, performance, interfaces, exclusions and recipient; any change requires renewed issue approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=50+0+20=70, gross=30, upkeep=5, net=25. High assumes currently repeated assembly of standard sheets. Low assumes bespoke work needs manual sheets plus upkeep. Technical definition and final checking retain time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyse bills and tariffs for energy history

steps.what: Gather energy bills and verify account, meter and historical period coverage
Read energy bills and tariffs into a historical usage table

loop.purpose: Extract fields only from nonstandard bill documents
loop.input: Scoped bills with original pages and account context
loop.output: Source-linked meter periods, quantities, units, rates and charges with uncertainty flags
loop.check: Auditor checks account and meter attribution, actual versus estimated reads, tariff applicability and credits as well as arithmetic totals
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction; unresolved period, unit or tariff ambiguities go to manual entry
loop.why_not_simpler: Use native structured exports and fixed parsers first; variable scans require bounded text interpretation

steps.what: Analyze historical energy usage and reconcile bill periods, credits and tariffs

tasks.design: Import structured bill exports into {DATA_PLATFORM} first and use a bounded extraction step only for remaining documents. Reconcile source-linked units, periods, credits and tariff meaning before using the history; meter feeds alone do not supply every billing field.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bills arrive in varied layouts and must be reconciled across periods and meters.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured imports and source-linked extraction can reduce transcription while leaving interpretation visible.
tasks.still_hard: Estimated readings, overlapping corrections, tariff changes and missing bills.
tasks.human_edge: Determine what the bill actually measures and which historical periods are comparable.
tasks.altitude: Less transcription, with unchanged evidence reconciliation responsibility.

reach.task: Clarify the energy baseline behind proposed measures
reach.learn: Meter scope, period comparability and tariff interpretation

evidence.claim: Ella Energy reads quarter-hour meter history and checks invoices, supporting energy-data and invoice-analysis capability without proving this extraction workflow's saving.
Source-linked bill extraction with human semantic reconciliation is an E1 model-knowledge design scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is collection, transcription and historical bill analysis, excluding baseline modelling and measure calculations. Reuse this checked dataset rather than recapture it in those tasks.

Supplier is the existing producer of account/meter IDs, billing periods, read type, quantity/unit, rate, fixed charge, tax, credit and billed total. Client supplies existing bills without a new structured-entry obligation. Auditor verifies coverage in s1, while s2's 18 remaining hours include extraction checking, manual entry of uncertain fields and source linkage.

Auditor produces the reconciled dataset in s3; missing periods or unclear tariffs stay unresolved until clarified. Test native export/import first. Six focal upkeep hours cover parser/schema changes and reconciliation exceptions; two data-administrator hours cover connector access.
research_questions: Does extraction save time after credits, estimates, units and tariff changes are checked against original bills?

already_counted.description: Extraction review and manual field correction

approvals.approved_version: Exact historical dataset revision, source bills, meter scope, periods, units, credits and tariff interpretations; changes require new acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=25+18+30=73, gross=27, upkeep=6, net=21. High assumes 60% less transcription after extraction review. Low assumes poor scans and complex corrections need all manual transcription plus upkeep. Coverage and tariff interpretation retain time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Quantify energy consumption and establish baselines

steps.what: Select comparable energy periods and verify the baseline measurement boundary
Quantify energy consumption using the selected periods and normalisation method
Evaluate quantified consumption and accept the energy baseline with limitations

tasks.design: Configure energy modelling software {OTHER} to aggregate and normalise checked consumption against the auditor's explicit baseline specification. Retain period selection, boundary judgement and model-fit review, stopping automatic results when coverage or fit is inadequate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comparable periods and normalisation settings are manually reapplied across calculations.
tasks.enabler_now: Native models can reuse a verified dataset and explicit calculation settings.
tasks.still_hard: Structural operating changes and baselines that poorly represent future use.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether the selected history is representative.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated arithmetic; baseline acceptance remains the auditor's decision.

reach.task: Understand the reference case for performance expectations

evidence.claim: OptiMiser calibrates energy models against utility bills, supporting energy baseline modelling capability without measured labour savings.

assumptions: Boundary starts with the checked bill dataset produced by the separate bill-analysis task. Bill extraction is counted there once; this task performs baseline selection, quantification and acceptance.

Auditor produces meter/building scope, chosen periods, excluded anomalies, units, weather series/reference, occupancy basis, normalisation method and version in s1. Its full 45 hours retain selection, field capture and gap investigation. Missing or noncomparable inputs require manual assessment rather than silently completed data.
Test native baseline tools first. The 25-hour saving is conditional on manual aggregation/setup today, never existing formula runtime. Five focal upkeep hours cover method and source checks.
research_questions: Can native quantification reproduce the accepted reference baseline across unusual operating periods?

approvals.approved_version: Exact baseline dataset, periods, exclusions, method/version, fit diagnostics and limitations; edits void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+0+30=75, gross=25, upkeep=5, net=20. High assumes manual aggregation and repeated settings can be replaced by native calculation. Low assumes existing native calculation or unsuitable data leaves all human work plus upkeep. Selection and acceptance retain time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Determine building-use patterns and energy needs

steps.what: Verify building use schedules and relevant heating, cooling and lighting data
Build monthly or annual energy-use profiles from verified time series
Determine building-use patterns and explain evidence for seasonal energy needs

tasks.design: Configure {BI} to display consistent monthly and seasonal profiles from verified time series and operating schedules. Keep causal interpretation with the auditor: aggregate consumption cannot automatically identify separate heating, cooling or lighting needs without supporting evidence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Profiles are rebuilt manually before patterns can be interpreted.
tasks.enabler_now: Native time-series grouping and charts can reuse explicit schedule and unit settings.
tasks.still_hard: Confounding weather, occupancy and mixed end uses.
tasks.human_edge: Check proposed explanations with actual building operation.

ambition.what: Review seasonal operating anomalies with the client at an additional agreed checkpoint

tasks.altitude: Less profile assembly allows more interpretation, without automatic building control.

reach.task: Discuss scheduling changes affecting building energy use
reach.learn: Distinguish observed patterns from causal claims

evidence.claim: Ella Energy uses quarter-hour meter history to identify deviations from normal use, supporting energy-pattern analysis capability without establishing end-use attribution or labour savings.

assumptions: Boundary is pattern profiling and interpretation, excluding the bill extraction and baseline quantification tasks. Shared energy history is captured once and reused; additional review demand is outside fixed-output savings.

Auditor produces building/meter references, timestamps and units validation, operating schedule, occupancy exceptions, weather basis and supported end-use labels in s1; its full 35 hours retain interview, capture and reconciliation. Building operator is the existing schedule-information producer; no new operator entry is imposed. Unknown end uses remain unassigned.

Test native profiles first. Five focal upkeep hours cover changing schedules and profile definitions; two data-administrator hours cover feed checks. Existing charts or system runtime earn no new saving.
research_questions: Do displayed patterns remain useful when unsupported end-use attribution is left explicit?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+0+40=75, gross=25, upkeep=5, net=20. High requires currently manual profile assembly. Low assumes native charts already run or inconsistent data requires manual profiling plus upkeep. Interviews and causal interpretation retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Potential gains concern specification formatting, bill transcription and repeated numerical presentation; technical content, baseline choice and interpretation remain human work.
reach: Discuss operating patterns with construction supervisors
role.ambitious_version: An energy auditor with traceable data and specification sheets who can spend more time explaining seasonal operating anomalies.
